Chameleon’s Camouflage Hunt

Age 4–5 YearsClass 31 · ScienceSkill Camouflage

Leaves, bark, snow — in every habitat, tap the animal that blends right in.

Play the science game ↓Print the worksheet ↓Play with a finger, a stylus or a mouse. Instructions are spoken aloud.
PLAY · CAMOUFLAGE

Chameleon’s Camouflage Hunt

Some animals hide in plain sight — that’s camouflage! Look at each habitat, then tap the animal that blends into it.

Who hides in the green leaves?

Who hides on the brown bark?

Who hides in the white snow?

Camouflage hunter!

The green grasshopper hides in leaves, the stick insect vanishes on bark, and the white rabbit melts into snow!

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

Camouflage is evolution a four-year-old can see: same colour = hidden. Play it at home — which toy vanishes on your sofa? Then look for hidden creatures on your next walk.

Illustration note: Loaded by content: the file named turtles-recycling-mission actually carries this Chameleon’s Camouflage Hunt artwork (the R2 export shifted files 20–30 by one slot). The snow photo already shows the white rabbit hiding — a lovely spoiler to point out.

Prefer paper? The Chameleon’s Camouflage Hunt worksheet prints the same experiment with room to think and draw — and a grown-up answer line. Printing never marks anything complete.
